Defines a heat wave as a prolonged period of excessive heat, often combined with excessive humidity.

The heat index is a measure in degrees Fahrenheit that indicates how hot it feels when relative humidity is added to the air temperature. Full sunshine exposure can increase the heat index by 15 degrees.
Heat cramps are muscular pains and spasms due to heavy exertion, often the first signal that the body is having trouble with the heat.
Heat exhaustion occurs when people exercise heavily or work in hot, humid conditions, leading to fluid loss through sweating. It can cause mild shock and, if untreated, may progress to heat stroke.
Heat stroke is a life-threatening condition where the body's temperature control system fails, potentially leading to brain damage or death if not cooled quickly.
Sun stroke, also known as heat stroke, is a serious condition caused by excessive exposure to high temperatures.

summary: An overview of earthquakes, defined as a sudden slipping or movement of a portion of the earth's crust, followed by vibrations.
An aftershock is an earthquake of similar or lesser intensity that follows the main earthquake.
A fault is the fracture across which displacement has occurred during an earthquake, with slippage ranging from less than an inch to more than 10 yards.
The epicenter is the place on the earth's surface directly above the point on the fault where the earthquake rupture began.
Seismic waves are vibrations that travel outward from the earthquake fault, causing most of the destruction during earthquakes.
Magnitude is the amount of energy released during an earthquake, computed from the amplitude of seismic waves, with each whole number increase representing about 30 times more energy.
